artifacts.title: CVE-2025-24071 NTLM hash leak to certipy shadow and ESC16 (Fluffy)
artifacts.starting_access: j.fleischman credentials with read/write access to the IT SMB share on a Windows Server 2019 domain controller
artifacts.outcome: Administrator via certipy shadow and ESC16 CA abuse
transferable_properties: an SMB share with write access lets you plant a malicious zip to capture NTLM hashes
CVE-2025-24071 leaks NTLMv2 hashes when a zip is decompressed, capture them with responder
certipy shadow auto extracts NT hashes for accounts with shadow credential access
BloodHound reveals the path from an owned user to privileged service accounts
ESC16 changes a user UPN to impersonate Administrator when the CA security extension is disabled
netexec adcs module finds ADCS enrollment servers

state_before.access: j.fleischman with IT share write access

observations: the IT share has READ and WRITE
it contains a KeePass and an upgrade notice about CVEs
CVE-2025-24071 leaks NTLM hashes when a zip is decompressed

hypotheses.statement: planting a malicious zip in the share leaks an NTLM hash when decompressed

selected_action.intent: run responder, plant a CVE-2025-24071 exploit zip in the IT share, and crack the captured hash

evidence.summary: captured p.agila's NTLMv2 hash via responder and cracked it with hashcat

observations: BloodHound shows p.agila can reach winrm_svc through service accounts
certipy shadow can extract NT hashes for ca_svc and winrm_svc

hypotheses.statement: adding p.agila to service accounts and using certipy shadow yields service account hashes

selected_action.intent: add p.agila to service accounts, sync the clock, and run certipy shadow for ca_svc and winrm_svc

evidence.summary: used certipy shadow to extract NT hashes for ca_svc and winrm_svc, then logged into winrm_svc via evil-winrm

observations: netexec adcs finds an enrollment server on DC01
certipy find shows the CA is vulnerable to ESC16 (security extension disabled)

hypotheses.statement: changing ca_svc's UPN to administrator lets the CA issue an Administrator certificate

selected_action.intent: update ca_svc's UPN to administrator, request a certificate, then restore the UPN

evidence.summary: requested an Administrator certificate via the UPN change, restored the UPN, and used certipy auth to retrieve the Administrator NT hash

observations: the Administrator hash works over WinRM

hypotheses.statement: pass-the-hash gives a shell as Administrator

selected_action.intent: connect with evil-winrm using the Administrator NT hash

evidence.summary: connected as Administrator and obtained the root flag
